rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb raised between two jussives may explain or substitute for the first result when both express the same action.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr's raised يغنها is also possible as an independent clause, paraphrased as the man who keeps relying on others does not enrich himself.
rows.anchor: من لا يزل مستحملا يكن من أمره ذاك ولو رفع يغنها جاز وكان حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Hutay'a's conditional, تعشو is raised as a circumstantial description, equivalent to arriving while blind.
rows.anchor: لأنه في موضع عاش كأنه قال متى تأته عاشيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil treats تلمم as an appositional substitute for the first verb, specifying that coming means visiting, like explanatory apposition between nouns.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a verse attributed through al-Asma'i from Abu Amr, يغدوا substitutes for لا يحفلوا, and arriving groomed explains their lack of concern.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن تأتنا تسألنا نعطك is allowed only as a slip followed by self-correction, since asking is not the same as coming; a comparable noun slip is مررت برجل حمار.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reads يضاعف as like the preceding result because increased punishment is the encounter with sin.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same explanatory substitution works when إحسان is specified by doing good, giving, or carrying the person.
rows.anchor: تفسر الإحسان بشيء هو هو وتجعل الآخر بدلا من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن تأتني آتك أقل ذاك is normally invalid because speaking is not coming, except as a tolerated slip like تسألنا.
rows.anchor: إن تأتني آتك أقل ذاك كان غير جائز لأن القول ليس بالإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When conjunctions such as ثم, ف, و, or أو link a second verb between the conditional jussives, that verb is also jussive.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These conjunctions share the second verb in the grammatical government imposed on the first.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه الحروف يشركن الآخر فيما دخل فيه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising is impossible under this coordination; تعشو was raised because it occupies the place of a circumstantial عاشيا, unlike a coordinated verb.
rows.anchor: لأنه في موضع عاش كأنه قال متى تأته عاشيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil allows accusative after ف or و by construing an implied أن and a nominal phrase, but says jussive is the proper construction.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jussive is preferred because the intended meaning is already jussive, and the nearest governing construction should apply without crossing into another syntactic domain.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative in Ibn Zuhayr's line is good because فيثبتها means the person slips unless he plants his foot.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After إن تأتني فأحدثك, the final verb can only be raised: the conditional sequence has ended, so the following clause is detached rather than coordinated within it.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With إن تأتني آتك فأحدثك, raising can start an independent clause, while accusative after ف or و is also possible as in the interposed-verb pattern.
rows.anchor: فأحدثك هذا الوجه وإن شئت ابتدأت وكذلك الواو وثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم does not license accusative through an implied أن as ف and و can; its meaning differs from و, and it coordinates rather than starting a new clause mid-condition.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between the conditional clauses ثم requires jussive, but after the whole conditional ends either jussive or raising is possible.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic examples show jussive after ثم in a completed conditional, including the fighting and turning-away clauses.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reportedly read يغفر and يعذب in the accusative after the conjunctions in 2:284.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising after ف is the standard choice when the preceding conditional answer is a nominal clause, because the following clause behaves as it would outside a condition.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the charity verse, نكفر is raised after فهو خير لكم because it follows an independent nominal clause.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: بعض القراء
rows.claim: Some readers raised ويذرهم by attaching it to the syntactic position of the preceding clause as a conditional answer.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative can match jussive when the whole preceding clause occupies an accusative syntactic position, as in the cited verse of poetry.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a conditional response containing لن or لم, a following verb is raised when it is not governed by that negative particle.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Match the response tense to the conditional: present condition with لا آتك and past condition with لم آتك; mismatched tense and negation are poor.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative after ف or و in a conditional sequence is weak and not the normal form, though somewhat more acceptable because the result depends on the first act.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يرتفع بينهما فقولك إن تأتني تسألني أعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry by al-A'sha supplies an accusative example; the construction remains nonstandard, and its sense resembles a promise qualified by إن شاء الله.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى فيما جاز من النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A response is jussive when it answers a command, prohibition, question, wish, or offer, because it depends on that first expression.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil explains these jussive responses by saying each opening expression carries the meaning of إن.
rows.anchor: هذه الأوائل كلها فيها معنى إن فلذلك انجزم الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples unpack the implied condition: come and I will come, tell me your house and I will visit, or if the wished-for person were here he would speak with us.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response يغفر لكم is jussive after the preceding invitation to believe and strive, which functions as the conditional premise.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أتيتنا أمس نعطك اليوم takes jussive only if the past visit is presented conditionally; if the speaker establishes that it happened, there is no conditional.
rows.anchor: أتيتنا أمس نعطك اليوم أي إن كنت أتيتنا أمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative constructions can govern a jussive, as in Jaber ibn Hunay's verse and the rajaz line متى أنام لا يؤرقني.
rows.anchor: ومما جاء أيضا منجزما بالاستفهام قوله

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabs pronounce the verb raised in متى أنام, construing it as a statement about sleeping without disturbance rather than a conditional response.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a command, raising is allowed if the next clause is independent; al-Akhtal's and an Ansari poet's lines illustrate this detachment.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil allows نعيش in the poem to depend on كونوا, or to be independent with the sense: be this way, since we live or die together.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jussive after prohibition is apt when avoiding the act causes the result; it is poor if the result is not caused by avoidance, while an independent raised clause or ف is fine.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trusted Arab's لا تذهب به تغلب عليه confirms the jussive pattern where the prohibited action would allow the consequence.
rows.anchor: وسمعنا عربيا موثوقا بعربيته يقول لا تذهب به تغلب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ذره, يقول may be raised as an independent clause or treated as a participle-like complement; the jussive instead marks a dependent result.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic ذروه examples contrast a jussive dependent verb with a raised independent one.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ائتني تمشي may be read as come walking, as a future jussive result, or with an independent raised verb.
rows.anchor: ائتني ماشيا وإن شاء جزمه على أنه إن أتاه مشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to strike a dry path through the sea, لا تخاف may be independent or describe striking without fear or apprehension.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قم يدعوك is raised when the call is not presented as caused by standing; a jussive gives that causal meaning.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal's كروا ... تعمرونهما means return while inhabiting the two places, with an independent raised reading also possible.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command مره يحفرها can take an independent raised verb; the rare construction مره أن يحفرها treats the verb as a noun-like complement, analogous to عسى.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command قل لعبادي governs يقيموا and ينفقوا as jussives; in the rare raised pattern the verb occupies the place of a noun.
rows.anchor: إذا كان جوابا لأمر أو نهي أو استفهام أو تمن أو عرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarafa's أُحضر is a verb in a noun-like complement position after الزاجري, illustrating the construction compared with rare raised verbs after commands.
rows.anchor: ألا أيهذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد, تأمروني is like saying هو يقول ذاك, understood as فيما تأمروني; it may also follow the pattern in Tarafa's line.
rows.anchor: تأمروني كقولك هو يقول ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In commands and prohibitions, the noun that the verb acts on is preferably accusative before the verb, following the default verb-first order.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commands and prohibitions require a verb, overt or implied, more strongly than interrogatives, which can be followed by nouns alone.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative pattern includes direct and prepositional objects, objects with a possessed item, أما constructions, and third-person commands.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A command may instead be built on a nominative topic, as in عبد الله اضربه and أما زيد فاقتله.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زيد فاضربه cannot be a topicalized subject, as shown by the ill-formed زيد فمنطلق; it can be accusative by an explanatory omitted verb or by an implied عليك.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an explicit or understood topic, ف before the command is good, as in هذا زيد فاضربه or الهلال والله فانظر إليه.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good sequence هذا زيد فحسن جميل shows that ف can link a clause after a topic; a Bedouin poem gives another command example.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هذا الرجل فاضربه works when الرجل is descriptive, while هذا زيدا فاضربه works when زيدا is an appositive or substitute.
rows.anchor: وتقول هذا الرجل فاضربه إذا جعلته وصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative اللذين يأتيانك may be accusative, raised, or a topic because a relative clause can take a nonverbal predicate introduced by ف.
rows.anchor: تنصبه كما تنصب زيدا وإن شئت رفعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative clause with ف has conditional force, allowing predicates such as فله درهم or فمكرم محمود, unlike a simple Zayd topic.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quranic relative clause الذين ينفقون ... فلهم أجرهم illustrates ف introducing the predicate of a construction with conditional meaning.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كل رجل يأتيك فهو صالح and كل رجل جاء فله درهمان work for the same conditional meaning.
rows.anchor: كل رجل يأتيك فهو صالح وكل رجل جاء فله درهمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Adi ibn Zayd's line, أنت is raised by an implied verb explained by the command فانظر, since the related element is nominative.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading makes أنت a predicate meaning you are the doomed one, as in saying a named person is destined for something.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون أنت على قوله أنت الهالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects analyzing أنت as a demonstrative construction, since one does not point the addressee out to himself or need to do so.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase طاعة وقول معروف likewise permits an implied topic with this as predicate or an implied predicate meaning better; it is not a fronted object.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication is grammatically like command and prohibition, so a named object is accusative in requests for forgiveness or well-being.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك اللهم زيدا فاغفر ذنبه وزيدا فأصلح شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Aswad's verse exemplifies the accusative in a supplication; raising is also possible under the same conditions as command, with matching disfavored cases.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أما زيدا فجدعا له and أما عمرا فسقيا له, accusative follows the omitted verb underlying the blessing expressions.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أما زيد فسلام عليه and أما الكافر فلعنة الله عليه are nominative because their topics are subjects.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quranic الزانية والزاني and السارق والسارقة are not fronted objects of the following commands; they follow an implied prior topic about revealed ordinances.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For الزانية والزاني, he supplies an omitted context such as in the ordinances, then the command follows after the nouns were raised.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السارق والسارقة follows the same implied-context analysis: the nouns are among what God has prescribed before the imperative appears.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما is likewise attached to an antecedent narrative or account.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same pattern can introduce Zayd or Amr after prior discussion or advice, with the command resuming the earlier topic.
rows.anchor: وقد يجرى هذا فى زيد وعمرو على هذا الحد

rows.speaker: أناس
rows.claim: Some readers used accusative for والسارق والسارقة and الزانية والزانى, a strong Arabic analysis, although the general reading is nominative.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative is the normal command pattern because verb-first order is obligatory more strongly here; unlike interrogative particles, commands have no independent particle that precedes the verb.
rows.anchor: والأمر والنهى يختار فيهما النصب فى الاسم الذى يبنى عليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative verbs can be omitted because their particles resemble conditional particles, but omission is poor with commands; command and prohibition clauses are inherently verbal.
rows.anchor: قبح حذف الفعل وإضماره بعد حروف الاستفهام لمضارعتها حروف الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object pronoun must remain explicit in زيدا اضربه because command and prohibition are verbal constructions and cannot dispense with that verb complement.
rows.anchor: فلا يستغنى عن الإضمار إن لم يظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vocative shortening of names such as منصور to منص deletes the ending and treats the preceding consonant like an augment, preserving the analogy of a final deletion and preceding sukun.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنك حذفت الآخر كما حذفت الزائد وما قبله ساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw of قنور and ya of هبيج behave like added letters in quadriliteral forms, originally appended to expand a triliteral stem.
rows.anchor: فصار قنور بمنزلة فدوكس وهبيج بمنزلة سميدع وجدول بمنزلة جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their analogy to radical-like letters is shown by nunation of a lengthening alif and by their ability to take further augmentations like unaugmented stems.
rows.anchor: فصار قنور بمنزلة فدوكس وهبيج بمنزلة سميدع وجدول بمنزلة جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because preceding ya and waw are treated like radicals or standard augmentations, they are preserved in vocatives; deleting two letters would excessively damage the root, as in مهاجر.
rows.anchor: فصار قنور بمنزلة فدوكس وهبيج بمنزلة سميدع وجدول بمنزلة جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a defective four-letter noun has an alif replacing a root consonant, its dual and plural take ya; even wāw-root forms shift because the larger pattern would make a corresponding verb use ya.
rows.anchor: أما ما كانت الألف فيه بدلا من حرف من نفس الحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A defective four-letter noun with an augmentative alif, such as حبلى or معزى, likewise forms its dual and plural with ya because an augmented derived verb would use ya.
rows.anchor: وأما ما كانت ألفه زائدة فنحو حبلى ومعزى ودفلى وذفرى
